extracted.intended_audience: researchers and prospective applicants to the CDMRP Lung Cancer Research Program (LCRP); lung cancer investigators seeking funding
extracted.subtask_description: Defines the Lung Cancer Research Program's vision, mission, target populations, and Areas of Emphasis that describe the research topics and gaps the program prioritizes for funding. Intended to guide applications and align proposals with program goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vision
rubrics_metrics.description: To eradicate deaths and suffering from lung cancer to better the health and welfare of Service Members, Veterans, and the general public
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States the program-level goal that funded research should ultimately contribute to eliminating mortality and morbidity from lung cancer across military and civilian populations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission
rubrics_metrics.description: Support and integrate research from multiple disciplines for risk assessment, prevention, early detection, diagnosis, management, and treatment for the control and cure of lung cancer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the scope of research the program supports—multidisciplinary projects across the cancer care continuum (risk assessment through treatment and cure). Proposals should align with one or more of these domains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biology and Etiology
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand the molecular mechanisms of initiation and progression to lung cancer; understand contributors to lung cancer development other than tobacco; understand the biology of metastatic/oligometastatic disease progression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Area of Emphasis: projects that elucidate fundamental biological mechanisms of lung cancer, non-tobacco risk factors, and processes driving metastasis or limited metastatic disease are priorities. Framed as addressing a critical gap that could reduce suffering and improve outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevention
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify innovative strategies for prevention of the occurrence of lung cancer(s) or subsequent primaries; identify innovative strategies for the prevention of recurrence or metastases from lung cancer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Area of Emphasis: proposals that develop or test novel primary or secondary prevention strategies (including preventing recurrence/metastasis) are prioritized as ways to lower incidence and improve survivorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detection, Diagnosis, and Surveillance
rubrics_metrics.description: Improve and expand approaches to screening and early detection of lung cancer; identify strategies for prompt detection and/or characterization of progressive disease.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Area of Emphasis: projects that advance screening technologies, early-detection methods, diagnostic characterization, and surveillance approaches—aimed at diagnosing lung cancer earlier or detecting progression sooner—are within program scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment and Prognosis
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify innovative strategies for the treatment of lung cancer, including overcoming resistance; develop or optimize biomarkers to assist with therapeutic decision-making; enhance the understanding, detection, and treatment of brain and leptomeningeal metastases in lung cancer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Area of Emphasis: supports work on novel therapeutics, resistance mechanisms, biomarker-driven treatment decisions, and improved management of central nervous system metastases to improve outcomes and prognosis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Health Outcomes and Survivorship
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and understand the long-term and cumulative effects of lung cancer and its treatment(s) on patients, families, and support systems with respect to the impact on quality of life including, but not limited to, physiological, psychosocial, cognitive, and financial effects; identify and understand impact of comorbidities on survivorship care in all stages of lung cancer; reduce differences among high-risk groups and populations with limited access to optimal clinical care and resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Area of Emphasis: prioritizes research on survivorship, long-term sequelae, comorbidity management, health disparities, and interventions to improve quality of life and access to care for high-risk or underserved populations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target populations and military relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus on Service Members, Veterans, and the general public; notes elevated lung cancer risk in military populations (higher smoking rates, deployments increasing smoking, and substantial Veteran risk).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program emphasizes research that benefits military and Veteran populations as well as the general public. Applicants should consider military/Veteran exposures, higher smoking prevalence, and access-to-care issues when framing significance and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Areas of Emphasis – selection rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: The following Areas of Emphasis are critical gaps in cancer research, care, and/or patient outcomes that, if addressed, will lead to reduced suffering from lung cancer and improved quality of life for Service Members, Veterans, and the general public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains that program priorities are defined as critical gaps whose resolution should demonstrably reduce burden of disease; applicants should map proposals to one or more of these gaps and articulate expected impact on suffering and quality of life.
